chunks: And with the first chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, who raised it (mursal), he said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon them both, used to say: "Woe to the one whose one (evil deed) overcame his ten (good deeds)."
And Abu Abdillah, blessings of Allah upon them both, used to say: "The defrauded one is he whose life was wasted hour by hour."

And Ali ibn al-Husayn, blessings of Allah upon them both, used to say: "Show despair from the people, for indeed that is true self-sufficiency. And reduce your seeking of needs from them, for indeed that is instant poverty. And beware of what you must apologize for. And pray the prayer of one bidding farewell. And if you are able to be today better than you were yesterday, and tomorrow better than you are today, then do so."

key_terms.المغبون: The defrauded one -- one who is cheated out of something valuable, here referring to one who wastes their life hour by hour
key_terms.رفعه: He raised it (mursal) -- a narration technique indicating the chain was raised without mentioning all intervening narrators
key_terms.صلاة مودع: The prayer of one bidding farewell -- praying with the devotion of someone who believes it may be their last prayer
key_terms.واحدته عشرته: His one and his ten -- referring to Quran 6:160 where one good deed earns tenfold reward, meaning one whose evil deed outweighs his accumulated good

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sajjad say about the value of time and praying as if bidding farewell?
ai.summary: Teachings from Imam al-Sajjad and Imam al-Sadiq on the value of time, self-improvement, self-sufficiency, and praying as if bidding farewell, with an allusion to Quran 6:160.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 6. With the preceding chains of narration, from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from ‘Ali ibn Hadeed from ‘Ali ibn al-Nu’man, who has raised the report (without intervening chain) to ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon him, who said:

"Woe to the one whose one triumphs over his ten (meaning the verse 160, Surah al-Ana’am: ’Whoever brings one good deed shall have ten fold the like of it and whoever brings one evil deed shall be recompensed only the like of it...’)"
And Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him used to say: "A defrauded person is one whose life is wasted hour by hour."

And ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon him, said: "Expect nothing from the others and that is true self-sufficiency, and minimize your needs from them, for being needful is instant poverty. And be cautious of doing things for which you may have to offer an excuse; and when you stand for daily prayers, do so as if you were offering the last and farewell prayers; and if you can manage to be better today than yesterday, or tomorrow better than today, then do so."
